data.reasoning: Report 2 (deepseek-v4-flash) successfully reviewed all 4 files and found the PKGBUILD to be a standard binary package downloading prebuilt tarballs from the official dkron-io/dkron GitHub repository with pinned SHA256 checksums. No code injection, no execution of fetched content, no unrelated network destinations. Reports 1 and 3 were inconclusive due to tool errors (API failures and parsing errors), not security concerns. Report 3 is advisory-only and doesn't count as a vote.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from tool failures, not security analysis. Report 1 failed with HTTP 400 errors on 3 of 4 files. Report 3's model entered a gibberish loop on .gitignore and failed to parse .nvchecker.toml. Only Report 2 completed successfully and found no issues. The 'inconclusive' verdicts reflect infrastructure problems, not package risks.
coverage_issues: Report 1: LLM API failures (HTTP 400) prevented review of PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, and .nvchecker.toml
Report 3: Model output parsing failed for .gitignore and .nvchecker.toml; .gitignore response shows model entered a repetitive loop/gibberish output
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, parsing errors, model loops) should be clearly distinguished from security findings in the verdict logic
When a model produces repetitive/gibberish output, the audit tool should detect this as a tool failure rather than marking the file as inconclusive
Advisory reports should be visually and logically separated from voting reports to avoid confusion about disagreement
